introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examinations. Pure Mathematics with Mechanics, Paper 3 (0765/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2021. Time allowed: three hours.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Mathematical formulae booklet published by the Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown: A uniform rod $AB$ of mass $2m\ \mathrm{kg}$ and length $4a$ metres is smoothly hinged at a point on a vertical wall. It is supported in a horizontal position by a light inextensible string attached to the rod at point $C$, where $CB = a$. The other end of the string is attached to the point $D$ on a vertical wall with $D$ above $A$ such that the string makes an angle $60^\circ$ with the wall. A load of mass $m\ \mathrm{kg}$ is placed at $B$ and the system is in equilibrium.
incertitudes: Question 3 : le sujet n'imprime aucune figure ; le modèle est déduit du texte : charnière en A (D est « au-dessus de A » sur le même mur), barre horizontale dirigée à l'opposé du mur, AC = 3a puisque CB = a, ficelle CD faisant 60° avec le mur (la verticale), donc 30° avec la barre. Cette lecture redonne exactement T = 16mg/3 imprimé en (a). Aucune valeur numérique de g n'est utilisée (résultats en m et g).

questions.enonce_markdown: Show that the tension in the string is $\dfrac{16}{3}mg$.
Find, in terms of $m$ and $g$, the horizontal and the vertical components of the reaction force at the hinge.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Resolve the forces on the rod in equilibrium, with $T = \dfrac{16}{3}mg$.

**Horizontal** (positive away from the wall): the string pulls the rod towards the wall with $T\sin 60^\circ$, so the hinge must push away from the wall with the same force:

$$H = T\sin 60^\circ = \frac{16}{3}mg\times\frac{\sqrt3}{2} = \frac{8\sqrt3}{3}\,mg \approx 4.62\,mg$$

**Vertical** (positive upwards): the hinge reaction $V$ upwards, the vertical component of the tension upwards, and the weights $2mg + mg$ downwards:

$$V + T\cos 60^\circ = 2mg + mg \;\Rightarrow\; V = 3mg - \frac{16}{3}mg\times\frac12 = 3mg - \frac{8}{3}mg = \frac13\,mg$$

**The horizontal component of the hinge reaction is $\dfrac{8\sqrt3}{3}mg\ \left(= \dfrac{8mg}{\sqrt3} \approx 4.62\,mg\right)$, directed away from the wall, and the vertical component is $\dfrac13 mg$ upwards.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine, to one decimal place, the angle which the reaction force makes with the rod.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The reaction at the hinge has components $H = \dfrac{8\sqrt3}{3}mg$ (along the rod, away from the wall) and $V = \dfrac13 mg$ (perpendicular to the rod, upwards). If $\theta$ is the angle between the reaction and the rod (the horizontal),

$$\tan\theta = \frac{V}{H} = \frac{\frac13 mg}{\frac{8\sqrt3}{3}mg} = \frac{1}{8\sqrt3} = \frac{\sqrt3}{24} \approx 0.0722$$

$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.0722) \approx 4.13^\circ$$

**The reaction at the hinge makes an angle of $4.1^\circ$ (to one decimal place) with the rod, above the rod.**
